name: Fendels
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying village in the Kaunertal, featuring the family-friendly ski area Fendels and an authentic charm.
beschreibung:
Overview

Fendels is perched on a sunny high-altitude plateau at 1,356 meters above sea level in the Tyrolean Oberland, within the district of Landeck. The peaceful mountain village sits nearly 480 meters steeply above the Upper Inn Valley floor, right at the gateway to the scenic Kaunertal valley. With roughly 280 inhabitants, this small municipality has retained its authentic, tranquil agrarian character without through traffic. From its sheltered south-facing slopes, visitors enjoy sweeping panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley towards the Lechtal Alps and the Samnaun group. Fendels charms holidaymakers by harmoniously blending mountain farming heritage with warm family-friendly winter sports and alpine summer recreation.

History

Traces of human settlement reach back into pre-Roman and Rhaeto-Romanic eras, reflected in the archaic origins of the village name. Fendels was first officially documented in 1288 in the land register of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol under the name Venels. During the late Middle Ages, Archduke Sigmund the Wealthy frequented Fendels for alpine hunting expeditions and endowed the community with its own resident chaplain. For centuries, the Cistercian Abbey of Stams held tithe privileges here, celebrated in the municipal coat of arms by the classic red-and-silver chequered band. Until the mid-twentieth century, the settlement remained secluded and accessible only via arduous mule tracks, until an automobile road was completed in 1959. The village center is dominated by the Late Baroque parish church of the Assumption, consecrated in 1778, housing ornate altars and the Late Gothic Wiesele crucifix. Higher up the mountain lies the historic Wiesele pilgrimage chapel, marking a famous seventeenth-century Marian hermitage.

Getting There

By automobile, travel leads via the Inntal motorway A12 and the S16 expressway to the Landeck-Süd/Reschenpass exit, following the B180 highway directly to Ried im Oberinntal. From Ried, drivers follow the winding L313 mountain road for approximately 4.5 kilometers into Fendels. Alternatively, visitors can park at the valley station in Ried and glide directly into the village center aboard the Ried-Fendels gondola cableway. Train travelers arrive at Landeck-Zams railway station, connected to international Railjet and Eurocity networks. Frequent regional buses on line 210 connect the station to Ried. Regional public bus transit is free for overnight guests carrying the local regional guest card.

Tips

In winter, the compact Fendels ski area features eleven well-groomed kilometers of slopes ranging from 1,350 to over 2,000 meters altitude, featuring Bibiland for beginners and a thrilling 4.5-kilometer natural toboggan run winding down to Ried. During summer, families enjoy walking to the Sattelklause adventure playground and relaxing at traditional alpine pasture Fendler Alm. Experienced mountaineers can undertake the ascent to the Anton-Renk-Hütte at 2,261 meters, offering prime views of the roaring 150-meter Anton Renk Waterfall and challenging fixed-rope climbing routes. A quiet woodland stroll leads to the secluded Wiesele chapel with magnificent valley views.
metaDescription: Fendels in Tyrol's Oberland: Sunny mountain terrace above the Inn Valley, family ski resort, Ried-Fendels cable car, toboggan runs and Anton Renk waterfall.
